A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SANN research and contain readable main text and Appendices A–G. Equations, proofs, figures and tables can be matched reliably across layout shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original linear-system experiments in Section 5, including Figure 3 and Table 1, and electrical-network reconstruction experiments in Appendix F.1, Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original linear-system results and the noiseless and noisy electrical-network reconstruction results in Figure 3 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The SANN architecture, Algorithm 1, MRNN recurrence, training objectives and semialgebraic transformer construction are retained. Corrections to projection notation and MRNN input descriptions do not establish a different computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate trained networks on 10-by-10 linear systems, demonstrate hand-crafted inversion on 50-by-50 systems, and evaluate 2-by-2 electrical networks with noiseless and 1% noisy inputs. Appendix G remains conceptual application coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the feed-forward network comparator. Appendix F.1 and Table 2 retain both the feed-forward network and Curtis–Morrow reconstruction algorithm, with no comparator added or removed.

E3.justification: Reported matrix sizes, strictly diagonally dominant sampling, network sizes, Adam training, residual and relative-error metrics, and electrical-network noise settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The hand-crafted Jacobi trajectory demonstration and the noiseless-versus-noisy reconstruction comparison are retained. No ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness scenarios or other supplementary empirical analyses are added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 3 continues to show trajectories for different input systems, rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains validation values 0.166 for the feed-forward network and 0.101 for SANN. Table 2 retains noiseless/1%-noise errors of 0.0157/0.0180, 0.0234/0.0273 and 2.49e-07/0.0469 for feed-forward, SANN and C&M respectively. Figure 3's trajectories and findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the direction-vector definition by projecting the full state derivative onto output coordinates. Appendix B.2 supplies the missing non-negativity condition for active neurons. These are limited mathematical corrections; the central expressivity theorems and proof constructions remain intact.

C1.justification: Both retain exact representation of bounded semialgebraic functions, including discontinuous functions, and demonstrations of trainability as their contributions. The introduction's change from 'computing' to 'representing' aligns with the exact-representation versus numerical-approximation distinction already stated in v1.

C2.justification: Both retain the numerical approximation caveat, bounded-image restriction, efficient-training challenge and caution against claiming numerical advantages. Appendix F's revised prose preserves the same explanation of noise sensitivity and learned-prior benefits.

D1.justification: Optimizer, loss-weight example, solver options, network descriptions and parameter counts are unchanged. No new implementation instructions, hardware or runtime information, or code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Appendix G.3 newly credits Furuya et al. (2024) for the transformer presentation and adds its reference. Section 2.1 adds Pierce–Birkhoff citations to already-listed works by Bochnak–Efroymson and Madden. Broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar, terminology and cross-references, polishes Appendix F's prose, and aligns Appendix C's Proposition 7 and Corollary 8 labels with the main text. Section and appendix organization remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds conference headers and revises the author layout. Existing material is reflowed: Example 6 is consolidated on page 4, Figure 3 moves to page 9, and Figure 4 moves to page 20. All six numbered figures and both tables retain their designs and content, apart from small caption edits.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and formal consistency through the projected direction-vector correction, completed activation-region condition, prose and cross-reference repairs, and added transformer attribution. These address localized ambiguities; the architecture, main theoretical arguments and empirical evidence remain essentially unchanged.
